heads.en: Prologue on the Intention of the Author

headnotes.la: … est Ecclesia: quia propter connexionem capitis ad corpus sacra Scriptura sub uno contextu, quasi sub eadem persona, aliquando loquitur de utroque; et de uno transiens ad aliud; verbi gratia, Isa. LXI
headnotes.en: …unt of the connexion of the head to the body, Holy Scripture, under one context, as it were under the same person, sometimes speaks of both; and passes from the one to the other; for example, Isa. LXI

headnotes.la: Quod enim dicitur hic
headnotes.en: For what is said here,

headnotes.la: etc., intelligitur de Christo, et quod subditur,
headnotes.en: etc., is understood of Christ, and what is added,

headnotes.la: etc., intelligitur de ipsa Ecclesia. Similiter Cant. 1
headnotes.en: etc., is understood of the Church herself. Likewise Cant. 1

headnotes.la: Cum enim dicitur,
headnotes.en: For when it is said,

headnotes.la: etc., verbum sponsae est frui sponso desiderantis, et quod subditur,
headnotes.en: etc., it is the word of the bride desiring to enjoy the bridegroom, and what is added,

headnotes.la: …: et ideo habet malos permixtos cum bonis usque ad judicium, in quo separabuntur hi ab illis; et ideo in sacra Scriptura aliquando mali commendantur cum bonis quibus sunt permixti: sicut Osee undecimo
headnotes.en: …good until the judgment, in which these will be separated from those; and therefore in Holy Scripture sometimes the bad are commended together with the good with whom they are mixed: as in Osee eleven

headnotes.la: Et e converso aliquando boni vituperantur cum malis, sicut Isaiae I
headnotes.en: And conversely sometimes the good are reproached together with the bad, as in Isaiah I

headnotes.la: Aliquando etiam in eodem textu exprimitur quid ad bonos pertineat, et quid ad malos, sicut Canticorum I dicitur
headnotes.en: Sometimes also in the same text it is expressed what belongs to the good, and what to the bad, as is said in Canticles I

headnotes.la: Verba sunt sponsae, quae ratione malorum in Ecclesia contentorum dicit
headnotes.en: These are the words of the bride, who by reason of the bad contained in the Church says

headnotes.la: sed ratione bonorum subdit
headnotes.en: but by reason of the good adds

headnotes.la: ad malos refertur: Cedar enim fuit filius Ismaelis, ut habetur Gen. XXV, a quo descenderunt Saraceni. Quod autem subditur,
headnotes.en: is referred to the bad: for Cedar was the son of Ismael, as is had in Gen. XXV, from whom the Saracens descended. But what is added,

headnotes.la: … referatur ad sensum litteralem tantum sicut et aliae. Circa quod considerandum quod eadem littera aliquando habet duplicem sensum litteralem; verbi gratia, primi Paral. XVII dicit Dominus de Salomone
headnotes.en: …the literal sense only, as the others are too. Concerning which it must be considered that the same letter sometimes has a twofold literal sense; for example, in I Paral. XVII the Lord says of Solomon

headnotes.la: …tur de Salomone ad litteram, inquantum fuit Filius Dei per adoptionem in juventute: propter quod Nathan propheta vocavit eum *amabilem Domino,* ut habetur secundi Regum XII Praedicta etiam auctoritas,
headnotes.en: …ing to the letter, inasmuch as he was a Son of God by adoption in his youth: on account of which Nathan the prophet called him *Beloved of the Lord,* as is had in II Kings XII The aforesaid authority,

headnotes.la: Quarta regula est de specie et genere, sive de parte ac toto, cum de uno transit ad aliud, et e converso, sicut Isa. XIII. Primo loquitur contra Babylonem specialiter, cum dicitur
headnotes.en: …e fourth rule is about species and genus, or about part and whole, when it passes from the one to the other, and conversely, as in Isa. XIII. First it speaks against Babylon specially, when it is said

headnotes.la: etc., et transit ad intelligendum verbum de toto mundo generaliter, per hoc quod subditur
headnotes.en: etc., and it passes to understanding the word of the whole world generally, by what is added

headnotes.la: Postea revertitur ad loquendum contra Babylonem specialiter, cum dicitur
headnotes.en: Afterwards it returns to speaking against Babylon specially, when it is said

headnotes.la: … vero loco ponit pauciores, dictas minutias omittendo. Tertio modo contingit in eo quod computatio annorum incipit in uno loco a priori termino, in alio a posteriori, sicut Gen. XV dictum fuit Abrahae
headnotes.en: …omitting the said fractions. In the third way it occurs in this, that the reckoning of the years begins in one place from an earlier term, in another from a later, as in Gen. XV it was said to Abraham

headnotes.la: …ista peregrinatione dicitur quod mansio filiorum Israel in terra Aegypti fuit quadringentorum triginta annorum, quia computatio hujus majoris numeri incipit a tempore, quo dictum fuit Abrahae, Gen XII
headnotes.en: …the dwelling of the children of Israel in the land of Egypt was of four hundred and thirty years, because the reckoning of this greater number begins from the time when it was said to Abraham, Gen XII

headnotes.la: …aac, quae fuit triginta annis post egressum Abrahae de Aram, ut plenius videbitur infra Exod. XII. Quarto modo contingit, eo quod Scriptura sacra loquitur de futuro per modum praeteriti, sicut Isa. IX
headnotes.en: …ty years after Abraham's going out from Haran, as will be seen more fully below at Exod. XII. In the fourth way it occurs, in that Holy Scripture speaks of the future by way of the past, as in Isa. IX

headnotes.la: …phetae infligenda populo, vel alicui personae, non secundum quod est in Dei praescientia, sed secundum ordinem causarum secundarum, ut pote secundum demerita hominum, sicut est illa prophetia Jon. III
headnotes.en: …evealed to the prophet, not according as it is in God's foreknowledge, but according to the order of secondary causes, as for instance according to the demerits of men, as is that prophecy of Jon. III

headnotes.la: …er eodem ordine gesta et facta scribuntur quo fiunt: et ideo quando praeponuntur posteriora, dicitur anticipatio: quando autem fit e converso, dicitur recapitulatio, sicut Gen. X de filiis Noe dicitur
headnotes.en: …n which they happen: and therefore when later things are placed first, it is called anticipation: but when the converse happens, it is called recapitulation, as in Gen. X it is said of the sons of Noe

headnotes.la: etc. Et infra eodem capite
headnotes.en: etc. And below in the same chapter

headnotes.la: etc. Et postea capite XI dicitur
headnotes.en: etc. And afterwards in chapter XI it is said

headnotes.la: …d praedicitur de divisione linguarum, dicitur per anticipationem. Similiter Gen. II, postquam Moyses cap. I descripserat creationem coeli et terrae, et distinctionem, et ornatum partium mundi, dicitur
headnotes.en: …f tongues is said by anticipation. Likewise in Gen. II, after Moses in chapter I had described the creation of heaven and earth, and the distinction and adornment of the parts of the world, it is said

headnotes.la: … loquens de uno, in eodem contextu transit ad loquendum de alio. Sicut Isa. cap. XIV loquens de rege Babylonis, qui erat diaboli membrum, transit ad loquendum de principe daemonum, cum subditur ibidem
headnotes.en: …ntext to speaking of the other. As Isa. chap. XIV, speaking of the king of Babylon, who was a member of the devil, passes to speaking of the prince of the demons, when there is added in the same place

headnotes.la: Et Ezech. XXVIII, loquens de principe Tyri, transit ad loquendum de diabolo, cum subditur
headnotes.en: And Ezech. XXVIII, speaking of the prince of Tyre, passes to speaking of the devil, when there is added
